producer: Check actual binary bytes against an exact literal expectation. Package separate specification/artifact knowledge objects, replay certificate, observed validation, supplied license/provenance and exact operation/validator source-byte witnesses. No search index is updated.
consumer: The caller independently pins the knowledge root, binary, expectation and semantic context. Fresh graph validity replays the built-in bounded independent binary decoder through the certificate boundary. The registered operation accepts only the exact task/input and a matching validated claim on that root, then resolves its actual binary payload from the checked closure.
acceptance: Freshly validate the exact output against the expected exports. Only an actual live operation plus output acceptance creates a reuse event; revoked, consumed, serialized or cross-task uses cannot do so.
scope: Closed i32 literal exports representing UInt32, Int32 or Bool. Existing validator restrictions and resource limits apply. Source-to-expectation binding and compiler preservation are not inferred.
implementationIdentity: Exact observed source bytes for the operation, binary decoder and certificate adapter. Shared boundaries and host runtime remain explicit assumptions; complete execution/input closure is false.
evidence: Three focused groups include real PSC-emitted unsigned/signed boundary and boolean functions, their actual derived expectation, certificate replay, accepted reuse and WebAssembly engine execution. Wrong tasks, modified certificates, stale context and substituted output reject.
